dedupe_keys.name: plans hillslope scale simulation tool for planning nature based solutions for water

description: PLANS is a Python simulation tool that helps water resources managers plan the expansion of nature-based solutions for water in watershed conservation projects. It simulates overland flow, infiltration and soil moisture at the hillslope scale using the TOPMODEL approach, which gives a spatially explicit picture of riparian wetland dynamics (variable source areas), so outputs such as maps of infiltration potential can guide where solutions are placed; the documentation positions it as an alternative to catchment-scale tools such as SWAT and InVEST. Users supply rainfall time series and maps of topography and land use for a basin of interest, so it covers any watershed with those inputs. It is developed by Iporã Possantti at the Instituto de Pesquisas Hidráulicas, UFRGS; the earlier plans2 framework (v1.0.0, 2022) was archived on Zenodo, milestone v0.5.0 was deposited in September 2025, and version 1.2.5 was published on PyPI on 15 September 2026. It is free and open source under GPL-3.0 (the Zenodo deposit lists CC BY 4.0), installable with pip or as a Windows application. Caveats: the documentation warns it is under active development and not a stable release, and results depend on the quality of topography and land use inputs. It supports climate adaptation and green-blue infrastructure siting studies; a related record is the Irish OPW NBS potential site identification maps.
